T0672.title: Slippage
T0672.definition: Slippage is the difference between an order's expected price and its actual execution price.
T0672.description: Slippage results from volatility, limited liquidity, order size, and transaction ordering. On decentralized exchanges, users set a maximum tolerance and minimum received amount so trades revert beyond the threshold. Frontrunning and sandwich attacks can deliberately increase victim slippage, making it both a market-structure metric and a signal for MEV and liquidity risk.
T0672.usageExample: The user set a 0.5% slippage tolerance, causing the transaction to revert when execution moved beyond the limit.
